subject: Post-demo: procurement clearance & signatory matrix — Crestline Therapeutics
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: procurement clearance & signatory matrix — Crestline Therapeutics

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the candid questions and the use-case detail. Quick recap and a few asks so we can move a commercial path forward with minimal blockers.

Key takeaways from demo:
- Primary workload: generation-heavy customer support automation (avg. 400k tokens/month).
- SLOs: 95th pct response < 350ms for critical routes; occasional bursts during campaigns.
- Security: Crestline requires SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, and single-tenant logging for PII payloads.

Immediate ask to help qualify procurement readiness:
1) Preferred payment method: PO vs. corporate card? (If PO, who signs and is there a purchase order workflow length?)
2) Budget owner / economic buyer: name and title.
3) Finance sponsor / approver: name and contact for billing/terms discussion.
4) Marketplace interest: do you prefer an AWS Marketplace flow vs. direct contract?
5) Any required procurement templates/clauses (we can accept your PO or push a standard Redwood SOW + PO).

Attachments: redwood-quote-crestline.xlsx (line-item quote + suggested payment terms).

Proposed next steps:
- If PO: please share PO template and target signing timeline.
- If card: confirm payer and payment window so we can prep an invoice.
- If marketplace: indicate PM/contact so we can initiate listing prep.

Would love brief answers on the five items above — if easier, loop procurement@crestline.com and we can set a short 30-min alignment next week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement clearance & signatory matrix — Crestline Therapeutics

Monica — thanks for the thorough follow-up and the demo. Short answers below to move this along: 

1) Payment method: We prefer PO for anything that goes through our platform team; corporate card only for ad-hoc pilots <$5k.
2) Budget owner / economic buyer: Laura Kim, VP Product (laura.kim@crestline.com).
3) Finance sponsor: Dana Ortiz, Finance Director (dana.ortiz@crestline.com). They handle payment terms and approval cadence.
4) Marketplace interest: We are open to an AWS Marketplace listing, but procurement would prefer direct for the first year while we validate usage.
5) Procurement templates/clauses: attaching our standard PO template. Key items: 30-day net payment, clause for SOC2 evidence within 30 days, redline on indemnity (we can provide legal contact on the next coordination call).

Attaching: crestline-po-template.docx (please confirm you can accept this format).

Proposed timeline: If Redwood can provide a formal PO-based quote by next Tue (6/15), we can route it internally and aim for signature by 6/25. If that timeline works, I'll get Dana looped.

-Paul
Paul Simmons
Director, Operations | Crestline Therapeutics
paul.simmons@crestline.com

Looping you both — Paul confirmed PO as the preferred path and shared their PO template. A couple quick internal notes and asks before we send back a commercial-ready packet: 

- Payment terms: they prefer 30-day net. We usually propose Net 30 for enterprise PO as well; fine to match for initial deal but flag for pricing if they ask for extended terms.
- Signature authority: Paul indicated Laura Kim is the economic buyer and Dana Ortiz will sponsor finance approvals; Paul may sign operationally for sub-$100k deals. We should validate approval thresholds.
- Marketplace: open in principle but want direct first year — low risk for taking the first-year direct route.

Action items for Monica:
1) Produce a PO-based quote (use attached redwood-quote-crestline.xlsx) with line items + one-sentence SLA and Net30 terms.
2) Ask procurement to confirm internal approval ladder (who signs >$100k, who signs <$100k).
3) Offer a short legal-sync slot (we usually do 30 minutes) to review indemnity/PII clauses.

If we can get the PO template redlined or confirmed as-is, we can attach a one-page master services summary and request Dana's approval. Recommend proposing 6/15 or 6/16 for the procurement + legal slot.

-ben
